metadata.title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
metadata.abstract: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.
